work.title: OPERATING MODEL
work.subtitle: A capability, interface and responsibility system
work.scope: A fictional Source Desk operating-model proposal. Four roles and five interfaces are conceptual; no named appointments, delegated authority, service commitments or actual organisational process are supplied.

pages.title: Start with the work the organisation would need to do.
pages.lead: Source Desk is a fictional concept for coordinating source-based explanations. Its operating-model question is how a defined task could move between roles without losing context or responsibility.
pages.body: An organisation chart alone cannot answer that question. This proposal examines capabilities, interfaces and review conditions. It establishes no actual team, appointments, operating authority or service commitments.
pages.detail: The model uses four functional roles and five proposed interfaces. Keep each responsibility linked to the relevant task rather than assuming that a title grants permission.
pages.question: What must remain clear when the work moves to another role?

records.label: Intent
records.prompt: Coordinate a bounded source-based explanation task.

records.label: Model scope
records.prompt: 4 conceptual roles and 5 proposed interfaces.

records.label: Authority boundary
records.prompt: No real appointments or delegated powers.

evidenceRows: 5 interfaces, 4 roles; no appointments or delegated authority.

pages.title: Trace a value flow that can return for clarification.
pages.lead: The proposed flow moves from a scoped brief to a draft, a source-status note, a review question and a revised explanation. The final handoff returns to the owner for another scope check.
pages.body: Return paths matter because review can create a question rather than an approval. The five interfaces are planning assumptions, not observed work or a guarantee that the process fits a real organisation.
pages.detail: Each output becomes the next interface’s input. This continuity makes the model inspectable without claiming that any actual handoff has happened.
pages.question: Where should an unresolved meaning return rather than disappear?

records.label: Start
records.prompt: Owner supplies a scoped brief to the author.

records.label: Review path
records.prompt: Draft, source-status note and review question.

records.label: Return
records.prompt: Revised explanation goes back for a scope check.

evidenceRows: 5 interfaces, 4 roles; no appointments or delegated authority.

pages.title: Map capabilities before assigning people.
pages.lead: The work needs intake, explanation, source coordination, review and revision capabilities. A capability describes something the proposed system must be able to do, not a named person or a software feature.
pages.body: One person might hold several roles in a real setting, but relevant responsibility and review boundaries must remain distinguishable. The model supplies no headcount, skill assessment or hiring plan.
pages.detail: Ask what artifact makes each capability visible and what information it needs from another role. Do not treat a list of capabilities as evidence that they are available.
pages.question: Which capability is assumed but not actually established?

records.label: Intake / explanation
records.prompt: Clarify the task and draft its meaning.

records.label: Coordination / review
records.prompt: Preserve source status and inspect the question.

records.label: Revision
records.prompt: Explain a change and return unresolved conditions.

evidenceRows: 5 interfaces, 4 roles; no appointments or delegated authority.

pages.title: Define interfaces as agreements about work.
pages.lead: An interface should name the sender, receiver, input, expected output and unresolved condition. A transfer of a file is not automatically a transfer of understanding or authority.
pages.body: The source register proposes owner to author, author to coordinator, coordinator to reviewer, reviewer to author and author to owner. No actual recipient, deadline or service agreement is supplied.
pages.detail: Use an explicit receiving question to expose a gap. Received should not mean verified unless that meaning is actually agreed and supported.
pages.question: What would let the receiver know what has and has not been checked?

records.label: Sender / receiver
records.prompt: A functional handoff, not a named appointment.

records.label: Artifact / question
records.prompt: Identify the version and requested next review.

records.label: Boundary
records.prompt: Receipt does not imply approval or delegated authority.

evidenceRows: 5 interfaces, 4 roles; no appointments or delegated authority.

pages.title: Carry context with the information.
pages.lead: A draft should travel with its working question, source status and relevant version. If a condition is unresolved, keep it next to the claim rather than only in an unrelated message.
pages.body: The operating model describes information needs, not an implemented system or permission to share material. Real access, retention and source-use arrangements require appropriate decisions in the actual setting.
pages.detail: A source-status note can say that a source is missing. It must not make a gap appear resolved just to produce a complete-looking handoff.
pages.question: Which piece of context would change how the next role interprets the draft?

records.label: Working question
records.prompt: Why this explanation is being prepared.

records.label: Source status
records.prompt: What is attributable and what remains unresolved.

records.label: Version
records.prompt: Which artifact the next role is actually reviewing.

evidenceRows: 5 interfaces, 4 roles; no appointments or delegated authority.

pages.title: Separate a proposal from delegated authority.
pages.lead: The owner could define the task scope, the reviewer could inspect within an agreed remit and the author could revise the explanation. These are proposed responsibilities, not granted decision rights.
pages.body: A real operating arrangement must establish who can approve, reject, refer or publish in the relevant context. Do not infer permission from a role label or from completion of a review worksheet.
pages.detail: The source register marks all delegation as not granted. This is a planning boundary, not an assessment of an actual organisation’s governance.
pages.question: Which decision needs a real authority that this document cannot provide?

records.label: Scope decision
records.prompt: Who can define or change the task?

records.label: Review decision
records.prompt: Who can judge the relevant claim and its evidence?

records.label: Release decision
records.prompt: Who can authorise the actual use or publication?

evidenceRows: 5 interfaces, 4 roles; no appointments or delegated authority.

pages.title: Allocate resources to capabilities, not just boxes.
pages.lead: A proposed system needs time, suitable source access and appropriate review capability. Resource planning should consider the work at the interfaces, not only the visible production step.
pages.body: No staffing levels, budget, workload or service duration are supplied. A role’s presence on the map does not establish its availability or imply that coordination and revision have no cost.
pages.detail: Inspect shared constraints and supporting work before proposing commitments. A real allocation needs appropriate responsibility and relevant information.
pages.question: Which interface could become constrained even if drafting capacity increased?

records.label: Time
records.prompt: Preparation, handoff, review and revision all need attention.

records.label: Information
records.prompt: Relevant source context must be appropriately available.

records.label: Capability
records.prompt: No actual staff availability or budget established.

evidenceRows: 5 interfaces, 4 roles; no appointments or delegated authority.

pages.title: Choose a review rhythm for a defined purpose.
pages.lead: A useful rhythm might include a scope check before drafting, a source-status check before review and a revision check before another decision. Each should answer a specific question.
pages.body: These are relative review points, not a calendar or a real meeting obligation. More meetings do not automatically create clearer responsibility. Decide what information should trigger a discussion and what can be handled through an appropriate artifact.
pages.detail: The model provides no actual meeting dates, response times or service levels. Keep the rhythm adaptable to the task and the relevant access conditions.
pages.question: Which review point would prevent a meaningful uncertainty from being hidden?

records.label: Before drafting
records.prompt: Is the task scope understandable?

records.label: Before review
records.prompt: Are source status and the receiving question visible?

records.label: After revision
records.prompt: What changed, and which condition remains open?

evidenceRows: 5 interfaces, 4 roles; no appointments or delegated authority.

pages.title: Handle a conflict at the relevant interface.
pages.lead: If the author and reviewer interpret a claim differently, preserve both the question and the relevant source before deciding who should resolve it. Do not let a status label conceal the disagreement.
pages.body: The model grants no escalation or arbitration power. A real concern needs an appropriate actual route and a clear remit. Distinguish missing information, competing interpretations and a decision that requires authority.
pages.detail: Record the issue at the task level without unnecessary personal information or an assumed judgement about someone’s motives.
pages.question: Is the conflict about a fact, an interpretation or who may decide?

records.label: Issue
records.prompt: The claim has competing interpretations.

records.label: Information needed
records.prompt: Relevant source, version and intended meaning.

records.label: Authority gap
records.prompt: No actual escalation or decision route supplied.

evidenceRows: 5 interfaces, 4 roles; no appointments or delegated authority.

pages.title: Evolve the model with a visible reason.
pages.lead: When an interface changes, record what work moved, why the change was proposed and how responsibility and source context will remain inspectable. Preserve the earlier map for comparison.
pages.body: This version contains a conceptual loop, not a tested organisational design. No actual performance improvement, governance approval or implemented change is reported. Use appropriate evidence before transferring the proposal into a real setting.
pages.detail: A cleaner diagram is not proof of a better system. Review the work and its conditions, not merely the appearance of the model.
pages.question: What evidence would justify changing this capability or interface?

records.label: Change record
records.prompt: Describe the proposed difference and its task reason.

records.label: Continuity check
records.prompt: Preserve the receiving question and responsibility boundary.

records.label: Implementation boundary
records.prompt: No real approval, rollout or measured improvement.

evidenceRows: 5 interfaces, 4 roles; no appointments or delegated authority.
